title: NimRTC Profile Schema v1.1
description: Scenario assembly profile (v1.1 — adds the `transport` block per transport-strategies.md). Strictly ADDITIVE on top of v1.0: every v1.0 profile loads unchanged; v1.1 profiles add the `transport` top-level key. The C++ loader (src/modules/assembly/src/assembly.cpp) reads the block into `assembly::TransportSection`. Five named use-case strategies (see transport-strategies.md §2) cover all known scenarios. The `strategy` field defaults to empty, in which case the engine compile-time default applies (equivalent to 'browser-call').

transport.description: v1.1 additive block — declares the transport strategy and the (media_stack, control_stack) pair. See docs/plan/transport-strategies.md §2 for the five named strategies.

strategy.description: Use-case strategy id. Empty string (or omitted) = engine compile-time default ('browser-call').

stack.description: Media-stack factory id. 'webrtc-classic' = libjuice + wolfSSL + usrsctp (default); 'raw-udp-arq' = bare UDP + ARQ (no SCTP, no browser interop); 'webrtc-quic' = v1.x WebTransport (not in v0.12.0).

max_p99_ms.description: Optional p99 latency budget. The Selector records the value but does not enforce it (v0.13+ may add a validator; see transport-strategies.md §6 #4).

control.description: Control-plane stack declaration. When `enabled` is false, control traffic rides the media stack's DataChannel (SCTP).

enabled.description: Enable a side-stack for the control plane. When false, control rides the media stack's DC (SCTP).

stack.description: Control-stack factory id. Only meaningful when `enabled` is true.

reliability.description: Reliability model for the control plane.
